checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan: add a seeded, deterministic fuzz harness that feeds generated text through every lexer/parser state machine and the full analyze pipeline, asserting termination and no crashes.

impact_assessment.why: State machines are only trustworthy if every transition is total; generated input explores combinations hand-written tests miss and can expose underflow or non-termination before users do.
impact_assessment.benefits: A reproducible robustness gate with no new dependency, plus fixes for any defect it exposes.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: test-only changes unless a defect is found; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: the generator must be seeded so failures are reproducible.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Fixed LCG seed, 500 generated cases per target, bounded assertions, golden regression for any found defect, full gate run before commit.

checkpoints.description: [2/4] Test-only: seeded 500-case generated-input harness; 690 checks green, no production defect exposed.
[3/4] Shell: no new I/O path; robustness is enforced inside the existing test gate; report documents the native-library guard interaction.
[4/4] README, ADR-011 and consolidated audit updated; 5/5 gates pass and 690 checks green.
Task 'knot-robustness-fuzz' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan: add pure CSV renderers for costs, hotspots and recommendations plus a 'knot csv' subcommand.

impact_assessment.why: JSON is good for tools but awkward for spreadsheets and issue attachments; a CSV surface makes the same deterministic data easy to sort and share.
impact_assessment.benefits: One more output format with no dependency, correct escaping, and the same stability guarantees as the JSON report.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: a new subcommand and --kind flag; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: rendering is pure and reuses the already-sorted analysis fields.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Golden CSV tests including embedded commas/quotes/newlines, CLI parse tests, full gates before commit.

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan: add a pure self-contained HTML renderer (stats, cycles, tables, DOT source) and a 'knot report' command that writes it at the edge.

impact_assessment.why: A terminal report is hard to share with people who are not running Knot; a standalone HTML file makes the same deterministic findings reviewable in a browser or CI artifact.
impact_assessment.benefits: A shareable, dependency-free report with no network resources and the same sort order as every other surface.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new subcommand and HTML output; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: rendering is pure with strict escaping.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Golden tests for HTML escaping and determinism, overwrite guard at the edge, full gates before commit.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan: approve and apply brand assets, fix the README tree, publish the public repository and push the verified tree.

impact_assessment.why: Publishing required a brand manifest and reviewed assets; the user authorized push, so the two resulting commits need a ledger task before the gated push can run.
impact_assessment.benefits: A clean delivery record for the publication commits and an explicit push through AIKit's gate.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: repository URL and topics; dependency: GitHub CLI authentication; concurrency: none; state: ledger staleness blocks push until a task is open.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Record a short task, run the gates, push through aikit.py push, verify HEAD equals origin/master.
